newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Baker presents new proposals in W.Sahara dispute.
newsitem.headline: Baker presents new proposals in W.Sahara dispute.

text.p: U.N. mediator James Baker presented proposals at talks between Morocco and its Western Sahara foes, the Polisario Front, on Tuesday aimed at breaking the deadlock over the future of the former Spanish colony.
Baker told a news conference at the end of two days of talks that the plan was intended to bridge the gap between the two sides who fought a 16-year bush war over the vast, mineral-rich territory.
The former U.S. secretary of state said the talks had been adjourned a day ahead of schedule to allow the delegations to return home to consider the proposals.
"We reached some bridging proposals. We can't go any further for now," Baker said after the talks ended at the 17th century Sao Juliao da Barra fortress near Lisbon.
Baker, asked by U.N. Secretary General Koffi Annan last March to spearhead a new bid to resolve the dispute, declined to go into detail.
Asked if he was more optimistic, he said: "Yes."
He said further progress depended on the response of both sides to the U.N. proposals.
If the response was positive, a new round of direct talks could be convened around mid-July, he added.

The United Nations successfully brokered a ceasefire in 1991 but has since failed to implement a proposed referendum on the future of the 250,000 square km (100,000 sq mile) territory because Morocco and the Algeria-backed Polisario cannot agree on who should be allowed to vote.
Baker was asked by Annan to evaluate whether the existing settlement plan was still viable or whether the U.N. had to adopt a new approach.
